title: Innovation in times of uncertainty
lede: Uncertainty is uncomfortable. But it is also one of the most reliable conditions for meaningful innovation.
content:
Uncertainty is uncomfortable. But it is also one of the most reliable conditions for meaningful innovation.

I had the pleasure of talking about how to effectively manage product innovation in times of uncertainty in collaboration with InProduct. The full talk is on YouTube.

Why uncertainty creates opportunity

When the rules of an industry are settled — clear incumbents, known user behaviour, stable business models — there is less room to move. Everyone is optimising the same playbook.

Uncertainty changes that. When the ground shifts, organisations that can move fast and experiment cheaply have an advantage over those waiting for clarity before acting.

The trap is treating uncertainty as a reason to pause. The cost of that pause is often higher than the cost of a wrong bet quickly corrected.

What it requires from product teams

Innovating under uncertainty asks something specific of product people:

  • Shorter feedback loops. You cannot afford to spend six months validating an assumption that the environment will invalidate for you.
  • Higher risk tolerance at the exploration stage. Not every initiative needs a clear ROI at kickoff. Some need space to find their shape.
  • Clear decision criteria. Uncertainty is not the same as vagueness. You still need to know what a good result looks like — and when to cut your losses.

The organisations that manage it well

What distinguishes the organisations that innovate well through difficult periods is not that they have more resources or more certainty. It is that they have built the habits — fast experimentation, psychological safety, clear ownership — before the uncertainty arrives.

Building those habits is not a crisis response. It is an investment made in the good times, so that the harder ones don't stop you cold.
